title: DrosoTracker: a web application with a self-calibrating thermal model for husbandry scheduling and lifespan analysis in Drosophila melanogaster
description:
DrosoTracker is a self-contained web application that predicts Drosophila melanogaster development from an explicit thermal-summation model and turns those predictions into a husbandry schedule.

The base model was recalibrated by linear regression of developmental rate against temperature on the author-verified transcription of Powsner (1935), over the linear range ~15-28 °C (T0 = 11.78 °C, DD = 116.38 °C·days, R² = 0.997, n = 13). On top of it, an optional two-level calibration learns from the user's own observations: a wild-type reference strain absorbs what is specific to a laboratory, and each genotype is then estimated against that baseline with a random-effects shrinkage estimator that accounts for measurement error and between-batch variability.

The application also derives husbandry tasks from each cross, analyses adult cohort survival with the Kaplan-Meier estimator and the log-rank test, and sizes lifespan experiments with Schoenfeld's formula. It runs entirely in the browser, stores data locally, works offline as a Progressive Web App, and is available in English and Spanish.

This release is the version described in the accompanying preprint. It includes the application, the R calibration script and the transcribed primary data, two simulation studies of the calibration estimator, and a dependency-free suite of 130 automated checks that run against the released HTML file.
